## Who this is for

AusPak is for a cricket analyst or fan who wants to compare how Australia
and Pakistan score runs and lose wickets across an ODI innings. The app helps
answer one question: **in which part of an innings does each side score
fastest and lose wickets, and has that changed over time?**

## Install

```{r}
#| eval: false
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-somya090997")
```

## Launch the app

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(AusPak)
run_app()
```

The app opens in a window or in your browser. Press the stop button in the R
console when you want to close it.

## What The Control Does?

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| Innings | Batting first (1st innings) or chasing (2nd innings) |
| Measure | Average runs per over, or average wickets lost per over |
| Show by | Three phases of the innings, or every individual over |
| Years | Keeps only matches that started in this range |

The two coloured boxes show how many matches each team contributes to the
current view. Gold is Australia and green is Pakistan throughout the app. The
section "What do the phases mean?" in the sidebar defines the phases:
powerplay is overs 1 to 10, middle is overs 11 to 40, and death is overs 41
onwards.

## How To Read the Results?

1. Start with the sentence under "What stands out". It names the phase with
   the biggest gap between the teams for the current settings.
2. Compare the gold and green bars within each phase. A taller bar means
   faster scoring, or more wickets if you chose that measure.
3. Check the match counts under each bar. A gap that rests on a handful of
   matches is weak evidence.
4. Change the years and see whether the gap holds in other eras.

For example, with Australia batting first across all years, the app shows
Australia scoring faster than Pakistan in the death overs. Narrowing the
years shows how much that gap depends on which matches are included.

If the chosen settings leave fewer than three matches for either team, the
app shows an amber message in place of the chart. Widen the years or switch
innings to continue.

## Use the function directly

The same summary the app uses is available as `phase_summary()`:

```{r}
library(AusPak)

phase_summary(aus_pak_overs, innings = 2, years = c(2010, 2020))
```

Read the `matches` column alongside the averages. Late overs come from fewer
matches because innings end early.

```{r}
head(phase_summary(aus_pak_overs, by = "over"))
```

## Limitations

- There are 45 Australia v Pakistan ODIs in the data, so narrow year ranges
  leave few matches.
- Phases are defined by over number only. Playing conditions have changed
  over the years, and rain-shortened matches are still grouped by over number.
- Wickets include every dismissal type, including run-outs.
- The app does not account for opponents' form, pitches or conditions.

Data: ball-by-ball records from [Cricsheet](https://cricsheet.org), accessed
through the cricketdata package.
